### Emergency Information Container
**LOCATION**

The EIB is generally kept in the Emergency Information Container (EIC). This is **located** at the **main entrance** to the site or building **adjacent** to the outer **warning placard. Larger** sites may be **provided** with **additional** containers at **alternative** locations, such as the **rear entrance.**

### Fire Sprinkler systems - Commercial systems
4 Main types of sprinkler systems
- **Wet** Pipe
- **Dry** Pipe
- **PRE** - Action
- **Deluge** System
- **Drencher** System

### Fire Extinguishers - Inspection and Maintenance
In general, fire extinguishers must be **serviced** at these intervals:
- **Six-monthly.**
- **Yearly.**
- **Five-yearly.**
- **After any use of the extinguisher.**

The date of each service should be indicated on the inspection tag attached to the fire extinguisher.

Firefighters **PASINN** must always check that the fire extinguisher is:
- **P**roperly maintained
- **A**ppropriate for the risk
- **S**ituated correctly (e.g. height, clearances, hung on a hook)
- **I**ndicated Correctly
- **N**ot obstructed by stored goods
- **N**ot damaged

### The 2 reasons to provide Entry Advice ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- For the attending officer to record the false alarm code
- Relevant details to the activation and the date of last test

### STATION ADMINISTRATION OPERATIONAL MANUAL
- Officer's Desk Book and Diary

### DESK BOOK
**The Officer's Desk Book is used to record information that the Officer in Charge on another shift may find useful.** Anything that happens during the course of a shift that may be relevant to other shifts is noted. It is generally only read by the Officer in Charge and may cover a range of topics.

Notations in the Desk Book may include:
- Materials received
- Keys to a new building obtained
- Faults reported
- Faults fixed
- Station maintenance
- Requests for assistance
- Incident information
- Movement of appliances/equipment
- Special events/tasks
- Safety issues
- Any other tasks achieved during the day
- Record weekly key check.

### OFFICERS DIARY
**The Officer's Diary is used for noting items tied to a day or a time.** This may include appointments such as a **FIRE ED** program, visits to schools and community education visits. Training dates and drills may be noted in the diary or any other information or upcoming events. Change of shifts or accrued leave is usually recorded in this diary for easy reference.

### FRV POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

### General Responsibilities ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- Participate in FRV scheduled workplace behaviour information sessions
- are familiar with this policy, and
- comply with this policy

### Who does this policy apply to? ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
This policy applies to all **employees**, including **current** and **prospective** employees, work **experience** and work **placement** students, **contract** workers and **commissioned** agents of the FRV, regardless of whether or not they work **full time**, **part time** or as **casuals**. It also applies to **everyone** FRV **employees** deal with in the course of their work.

### When does this policy apply?
- dealing with members of the **public**
- work-related **functions**
- **conferences**; and
- **other social activities** involving employees

### WORKPLACE BULLYING
Workplace bullying is **repeated**, **unreasonable behavior** towards an **employee, client, contractor, customer** or *other* **external party** that creates a **risk** to their **health** and **safety**.

### SEXUAL HARASSMENT
**3 Actions**

A person sexually harasses another person if they:
- Make an "**unwanted sexual advance**"
- Make an "**unwelcome request for sexual favours**"; or
- Engage in any other "**unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature**"

### DEFINITION ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
Sexual harassment is the **UNWANTED, UNINVITED BEHAVIOUR** which is **OFFENSIVE** from the view point of the **PERSON BEING HARASSED**, it does not matter that the offender **DID NOT MEAN OR INTEND TO SEXUALLY HARASS** the other person. In other words, an offender's **INNOCENT INTENT IS IRRELEVANT.**

### VILIFICATION ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
Is a public act that incites **HATRED, CONTEMPT** or **RIDICULE** of a person or group on the grounds of **RACE** or **RELIGION**

### ORG 109 - Work Health & Safety Incident Management
### POINT 5 RESPONSIBILITIES
5. Officer/s In Charge (OICs) /Supervisors OICs/Supervisors are responsible for:
- Completing the FRVSafe initial report or ensuring that the reporting / injured / affected worker has completed the FRVSafe initial report within 24 hours of an incident occurring
- Completing an FRVSafe initial report on behalf of a visitor, contractor, subcontractor or member of the public who is affected by an incident / near miss / hazard
- Notifying their Commander or Manager if the incident is notifiable as per Appendix A or if the risk rating is rated 'high' or above.

### POINT 6.1 IMMEDIATE RESPONSE
- **Eliminate or isolate** any remaining hazards at the incident site which may have the potential to cause any immediate further harm, if safe to do so.
- **Initiate first aid treatment** (if required). Consider the need for further medical treatment. Fire Rescue Victoria Page Number: 5 of 8 THIS DOCUMENT IS UNCONTROLLED WHEN PRINTED
- **Immediately notify** Supervisor/Officer in Charge (OIC). Cont...

- Supervisor/OIC must immediately notify the relevant Manager/Commander unless the hazard / incident is of a minor nature (e.g. a facility issue requiring rectification)

### APPENDIX A
### INCIDENTS REQUIRING NOTIFICATION TO WORKSAFE:
As per section 37 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Vic) – any incident that results in the following requires **immediate notification to WorkSafe:**
- the **death** of a person; or
- a person requiring **medical treatment within 48 hours of exposure** to a substance; or
- a person requiring **immediate treatment as an in-patient in a hospital**; or
- a person requiring **immediate medical treatment** for:
- any other injury to a person or other consequence prescribed by the regulations.
- any incident that exposes a person in the immediate vicinity to an immediate risk to the person's health or safety through the following

### ORG 133 - WorkCover
### RESUMPTION OF DUTY
All staff returning to work following time off for a work related injury are;
- to obtain a **WorkCover Certificate of Capacity – Full Clearance** for pre-injury duties before resuming their pre-injury work. This can be included in a **Certificate authorising time off**
- FRV, under its regulations, may also request operational staff to attend the **Brigade Medical Services (BMS)** to confirm fitness for duty before resuming work.

### REPORTING - SO Responsibilities
### FRV SAFE REPORT
The immediate OIC/Supervisor of the claimant is responsible for-
- Ensuring the initial FRVSafe report is completed **as soon as practical** and assigning the FRVSafe report to an appropriate investigator
- Completing the initial FRVSafe report when **a claimant is unable to do so** and assigning to an **appropriate investigator**
- Reporting to the FRV workcover claim section any **additional information** that may assist in making a decision concerning the acceptance of liability.

### 32 POWERS OF ACCESS ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (wordfill)
Within the Fire Rescue Victoria fire district FRV or any person **authorized** for the purpose by FRV shall at all **reasonable** times have free access to any **land** building **premises** or other **place** for the purpose of ascertaining whether this Act and the regulations and any other law relating to—
- (a) the storage of **explosives**;
- (b) the storage of **radioactive substances**;
- (c) the storage of **inflammable liquids** or **substances**; and
- (d) the prevention of **fire** or the protection of **life** or **property** in the case of fire—

are being complied with

- Any call for assistance at **fire, accident, explosion** or **other emergency**

### 32AA DUTY TO WARN THE COMMUNITY 'hey hey'

### 32B ACTION ON ALARM OF FIRE
We can do anything 'within reason' to get the job done.

### 32B 3(C) MAY FOR THE PURPOSE OF DEALING WITH ALARM OF FIRE ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (wordfill)
- i. Any **land, building, structure, vessel** or vehicle to be **entered** upon or into (if necessary by force), taken possession of, **shored up pulled down**, otherwise destroyed or removed
- ii. Any **vehicle** or **equipment** to be taken through upon or into any land building structure vessel or vehicle
- iii. **Water** to be **shut off** from any main pipe or other source of supply in order to obtain a greater pressure or supply of water, and
- iv. Any **road water railway** or tramway to be closed to traffic or any main pipeline conduit or conductor of **gas, electricity, oil** or any source of **power, fuel** or **energy** to be shut off

### 54 Damage done to be within policy 'Sec 54 Kick in the door'
- Damage caused within the powers of this act are deemed to be damage by fire within the meaning of any **fire insurance policy** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

### 54A IMMUNITY FROM CERTAIN LIABILITIES 'sec 54A immunitAY' ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Not personally liable because actions by members in good faith

### 58 REMOVAL OF PERSONS FROM BURNING PREMISES (Sec 58 Get out mate)
A member of a unit or a **police officer** may order **any person** who is not a member of a unit or who is not acting under the control or direction of a member of a unit to **withdraw** from any premises then burning or which are threatened by fire.

(1A) A person **must comply immediately** with an order given to the person under subsection (1).

(2) If such person neglects or **refuses** to so withdraw he may be forcibly removed by order of any such member. Cont...

(3) Nothing herein contained shall authorize the removal from any such premises of any person having any **pecuniary interest** therein or in any goods or valuables whatsoever thereon

### 59 RIGHTS TO WATER 'Sec 59 Water is mine'
- for any purpose of extinguishing **fire**
- for purpose of **drill, competition** and **practice conducted**

### 61 POLICE to aid Units 'Sec 61 comes with a gun' ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
For the purpose of subsection (2), police officers may—
- (a) **close** any **street in** or **near** which a fire is burning; and
- (b) of their own volition or at the request of the senior member of the operational staff at the scene, **remove** any **persons** who **interfere** by their **presence** or otherwise with the **operations** of the unit.

### 78A Offences by Officers or Members (GGNIG) ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
A member of the operation staff who is-
- a) **G**uilty of any breach of **REGULATIONS**
- b) **G**uilty of any **MISCONDUCT**
- c) **NEGLIGENT** or **CARELESS** in the **DISCHARGE** of his/her duties
- d) **INEFFICIENT** or **INCOMPETENT** and such inefficiency or incompetence arises from causes within his/her own control arises
- e) **G**uilty of any **DISGRACEFUL** or **IMPROPER** conduct

shall be guilty of an offence.

### FRV (General) Regulations 2020
- REG 12 – Prohibitions on Members

### An operational staff member must not-
**D E W W W A B B**
- a) **DISOBEY** or **FAIL** to carry out a **GENERAL ORDER** or any **LAWFUL ORDER** in course of his or her duty whether the order is in writing or not; or
- b) **EXCEED** or **MISUSE** the member's authority; or
- c) **WILFULLY** cause **or allow Loss**, **Damage or Injury** to occur to any **PERSON** or **PROPERTY**; or
- d) **WHEN** on duty, partake in or be under the influence of or affected by any **INTOXICATING** liquor, **NARCOTIC**, **HALLUCINOGEN, MEDICATION** or substance that could or likely to **impair, limit** or affect the member's **performance of duty**; or
- e) **WHEN** on duty have any of the substances referred to in paragraph (d) in his or her possession or at the **WORKPLACE;** or
- f) **ACT** in a manner that is likely to bring **DISCREDIT** to the reputation of the **BOARD** or **DIMINISH** public confidence in it; or
- g) **BE** found guilty of having committed an **INDICTABLE** offence when on duty; or
- h) **BE** found guilty of having committed an indictable offence under Division 2 of Part 1 of the Crimes act 1958 when not on duty if the offence involved **DISHONESTY**, **CORRUPTION**, **INTENT TO DECEIVE** or **DEFRAUD** or **TRESPASS**
